findings.title: Embedded post author-link lightness values are inverted
findings.body: The original color for links inside `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so in light theme the link is lightened 70% instead of 30%, and in dark theme it is lightened only 30% from `$secondary` instead of the corresponding 70%. This lowers contrast in both themes, especially against dark backgrounds, making expanded-post author links hard to read. It should preserve 30% for the light branch and use 70% for the dark branch.

findings.title: Custom message length hint uses reversed lightness values on mobile
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, a light hint color. The replacement uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for the light branch and `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for the dark branch, reversing both. This makes the hint much darker than before in light theme and brighter than intended in dark theme, and it is inconsistent with `desktop/modal.scss`, which uses the expected 70/30 mapping. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 heading lightness was changed accidentally
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new expression uses 50% for both branches, so in light theme the heading becomes much lighter than before, and in dark theme it uses 50% from `$secondary` rather than the expected 80% counterpart. This also differs from the desktop topic-map h3 rule, which correctly maps 20% to 80%. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`.

findings.title: Group member name color no longer preserves the original 30% lightness
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which changes the light-theme color from 30% to 50% and uses only 50% from `$secondary` in dark theme instead of the corresponding 70%. The name becomes noticeably less distinct than before. It should preserve the light value and use the 70% dark counterpart.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color no longer preserves the original 30% lightness
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, changing the light-theme color from 30% to 50% and using 50% from `$secondary` in dark theme instead of the expected 70%. This makes the member name lighter than before and inconsistent with the same selector on desktop. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Category badge-notification still uses $primary in dark themes
findings.body: The PR converts the muted topic-list colors in this file to `dark-light-choose`, but `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. Since `$primary` is light in dark themes, this badge count is lightened further instead of being derived from `$secondary`, so the original dark-theme contrast issue remains for category badge notifications. It should be converted like the surrounding rules, e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`.
